reading.title: The cheaper supplier
reading.text:
Last March, a small furniture company received an offer that looked impossible to refuse. A new supplier promised the same components at 22% below their current price, with delivery in three weeks instead of five.

The operations manager, Ivana, did not sign immediately. She asked for a sample batch and sent it to the workshop for testing. The parts arrived on time and looked identical to the ones they already used.

What changed her mind was a single question she put to the workshop foreman: how long does it take to fit one? The answer was eleven minutes, against seven for the current parts. The holes had been drilled a fraction off centre, so every piece needed adjusting by hand.

Across a year, those four extra minutes came to more than 600 hours of labour, considerably more than the 22% saved on the parts themselves.

Ivana kept the original supplier and negotiated a 6% discount by showing them the competing offer. The whole exercise took three weeks and cost nothing but a sample batch.

She now applies the same rule to every quote the company receives: the price on the invoice is never the full price. What matters is what a thing costs once it is in your hands.

questions.q: What did the new supplier promise?
Why did Ivana ask for a sample batch?
options: To test the parts before committing
To push the price down further
To delay the decision on purpose

options: They arrived in the wrong colour

questions.q: How much extra labour did the new parts create over a year?
What did Ivana do in the end?
options: Stayed with the original supplier at a lower price
Signed with the new supplier anyway

questions.q: "An offer that looked impossible to refuse" suggests the offer seemed
What does "the price on the invoice is never the full price" mean here?
options: The real cost includes what a thing costs to use
Prices tend to rise after signing

questions.q: What does the passage imply about the sample batch?
options: It was a cheap way to avoid an expensive mistake
It wasted three weeks the company could not spare
It should have been considerably larger
It proved the parts were dangerously faulty
